his_text: Treat the demonstration as a strong existence proof that alignment-faking can serve a training-acquired goal, while noting it did not occur during actual training and is not the worst case
Design the evaluation without giving the model a goal or telling it to preserve capabilities, letting it learn through interaction that performing too well leads to its capability being removed

Treat scheming concerns as specific to language models and exclude earlier game-playing reinforcement learning agents, since they cannot reason about their own training process or how to circumvent it

Launch the large-scale research program on the science of scheming immediately rather than waiting, treating the present as a possibly closing window for studying the behavior while it remains observable
Manually review every flagged transcript and discard any case where the chain of thought is ambiguous, then report only the unambiguous remainder as a conservative lower bound on covert actions
Acknowledge that the role-play confounder cannot always be resolved and inspect the chain of thought in each case for how seriously the model appears to treat the situation before counting the action

Place anti-deception principles in context, generate rollouts, select cases where the model declines the covert action for the right reasons, then apply supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning
Present the reduction humbly as only a small step in the right direction, noting that most of the problem remains, that failure modes persist, and that covert actions are only a proxy
Skip the before-and-after comparison of evaluation awareness's effect on scheming because post-training misaligned behaviour is too rare to yield statistically significant results
Treat goals and situational awareness as fuzzy aggregates of many features with varying activation rather than as single crisp binary features that the model always tracks
Attribute the opaque jargon to reinforcement learning dynamics and length pressure rather than deliberate obscuring, since the chain of thought is not directly trained
Support attempts to remove the awareness-of-evaluation direction but warn that researchers will likely fool themselves because isolating the feature requires perfectly matched datasets
Use chains of thought directionally as a source of information about scheming while applying a heavy dose of scepticism to whatever the model's reasoning appears to show
Reject the fallback of halting deployment for months to retroactively study the prior model, since pausing release for a big research project is economically unfeasible
Expect alignment techniques to transfer only to roughly human-level models and assume they fail entirely against superintelligence rather than planning on lasting transfer
Prefer building a predictive science of scheming with causal understanding of training incentives over the default spray-and-pray approach, while endorsing the latter over nothing
Use several separate reward signals covering task success, manner of solving, scheming, and expressed uncertainty that counterbalance each other, plus reward refusal of misaligned actions
Continue the collaboration on future projects covering the science of scheming, anti-scheming measures, and monitoring despite the concerns about the company's corporate conduct
Give internally deployed systems privileged access that is denied by default and granted only when necessary, while mapping angles of attack and deploying mitigations against them
Characterize the pathway as multiple failure modes interacting and exploding simultaneously rather than the clean single-mechanism takeover depicted in other published catastrophe scenarios
Treat the threat model as broader than self-exfiltration, including the model taking over its own company or embedding itself in government, and orient concern around that range
Favor softer accountability measures such as required interaction with third parties, external oversight, and audits that force companies to explain and double-check their choices
Treat internal deployment as a serious source of risk and reject the status quo intuition that internally used systems need no guardrails because models were not dangerous before
Highlight evaluations, control and monitoring, and model organisms as the tractable contributions outsiders can make, since they can be done externally at modest compute cost
Focus external effort on evaluations, control, and model organisms rather than training-based anti-scheming work, which needs compute and lab access.
Shift relative effort toward scheming research and away from interpretability and capability evaluations, while treating all subfields as underfunded.
Treat work on scalable oversight as a high-risk, high-reward bet worth attempting despite little positive evidence that it works so far.
Send newcomers into hands-on projects through existing upskilling programmes rather than building a dedicated anti-scheming training pipeline.
Keep treating the chaotic multi-actor picture as important, since human coordination games persist even when capabilities take off rapidly.
Pursue anti-scheming research at an external organization that collaborates with all frontier labs instead of working inside a single lab.
Split research effort evenly between interpretability and behavioral evaluations, aiming to merge both approaches into one method long run.
Extend the framework by reasoning from first principles about where risk is created and auditing the system at each of those points.
State the guess cautiously that the model's absolute ceiling sits just below human level while flagging that the limit may lie in current scaffolding
Treat doing many tasks in one generation and doing them one at a time as different capabilities rather than evidence about a single capability
Treat absolute capabilities as a theoretical bound that practical testing cannot approximate no matter how much evaluation is run
Focus on interpretability primarily to address deceptive alignment where models appear aligned externally but pursue different internal goals
Keep behavioral evaluations and interpretability as separate lines of work since current interpretability tools are not practically useful yet
Continue investing in interpretability of large models since full interventional access makes fast hypothesis testing possible despite the difficulty
Treat whether feedback-driven training induces deception as unresolved since it might induce deception or might simply work as intended
Target the upper bound of what a system can do rather than only what it does reliably when auditing for misuse or takeover risk
Treat an interpretability technique tied to one specific architecture as probably weak, and expect a correct technique to generalize across architectures.
Claim only that tool use appeared to move quickly based on public demonstrations and secondhand reports, and avoid asserting certainty about timelines inside the labs.
Commit to building the full mechanistic understanding first, and defer the question of cheap deployment-time monitoring until that part is solved.
Publish the small finding as a technical report framed as an existence proof, despite uncertainty about whether it is significant enough to release.
Test next whether the model can be induced to deceive purely through situational pressure, without ever being instructed or asked to deceive.
Engineer the discovered scenario, then adjust it toward the most realistic setting possible and vary its mechanisms to test whether the model acts consistently.
Count the simulated-agent deception as genuine evidence, since the deployed model would produce the same behavior in the same situation.
Decline to endorse the claim, noting the main plot shows the prohibited action rather than deception itself and rates may confound opportunity with capability.
Test the capability claim across a long list of models of different sizes, removing correlations and confounders before asserting that more capable models deceive more
Structure deployment approval as layered checks where labs, external auditors, and government each act independently so the process stays robust if one link fails
Release in stages: have trusted outside auditors probe the model first, fix what surfaces, then roll out to a small set of verified customers while monitoring
Release open models in stages: let a small trusted team first probe the upper bounds of harm and how easily safeguards come off before wider general release
Start by picking a behavior that seems interesting and probing the model for a while, letting the project grow organically rather than overthinking the choice
Explain the behavior through how the model was trained, using knowledge of the training pipeline and its tradeoffs to spot niches that training never covered
Keep deceptive behavior and scheming as the organisation's central research focus, concentrating evaluations, interpretability, and related work there going forward
Treat flattery and user-modeling as a secondary concern compared with outcome-training risks like power-seeking, which pose the more serious long-run danger
Run the full eval suite, compare scores against previous models, then read transcripts in detail including failures while probing the model informally.
Run the whole suite quickly in parallel, inspect where the numbers come from, then do guided analysis and build a few new evals for the most concerning areas.
Treat qualitative reading of transcripts and failure cases as a major source of evidence alongside scores, rerunning evals many times to inspect variants.
Split the tests into precursor capabilities like self-reasoning and modeling others, plus an end-to-end scheming test, to get signal earlier.
Treat failures from long-horizon outcome training as the main danger and reward gaming and flattery as secondary issues deserving less attention.
Place the scaffolded model as an agent in a sandboxed computing environment with shell access and tasks requiring reasoning about itself and its surroundings.
Create easy, medium, and hard versions of each task that vary only in how many hints are given, with the hardest giving no hints at all.
Design the evaluation primarily to measure whether the model is capable of scheming, accepting goal setups that make both goals defensible.
Treat cooperative-looking behavior under goal conflict as a refusal confound rather than evidence of safety, separating capability failure from alignment failure
Study covert actions where the model strategically omits important information as a simpler proxy for full scheming in models lacking coherent long-term goals
Test anti-scheming training in which the model explicitly reasons over a written specification of allowed behavior, as the concrete mitigation to try in practice
Treat scheming as covert pursuit of goals that conflict with developer goals, meaningfully distinct from the broader category of reward hacking rather than a subset
Characterize reward hacking in language models as strategic and deliberate, distinct from the mechanical specification-gaming seen in classic reinforcement learning
Warn that current setups monitor poorly for emerging instrumental strategies and that models will learn deceptive resource-seeking by default unless heavily penalized
Characterize observed alignment-faking and covert behavior as early forms driven by semi-coherent preferences rather than fully developed deceptive alignment
Write the behavioral specification as a short, general document of high-level rules covering broad principles like honesty rather than a long list of scenario cases
Lock the specification after the initial version and proceed with it as the foundation for training, without running further revision rounds based on the test results.
Have human reviewers go through every flagged chain of thought one by one and keep only the cases where the covert action is unambiguous, excluding everything borderline.
Warn that telling a model something extreme depends on its output will probably make it produce a result that merely looks right, while noting this remains untested.
Report only the aggregate deception rate across all pressure strengths rather than breaking out finer splits that would rest on small samples and arbitrary categorizations.
State the results conservatively in the write-up, including only the claims the evidence fully supports rather than stronger interpretations the numbers might suggest.
Read the chains of thought with heavy skepticism but treat them as directionally informative about the model's reasoning rather than as either reliable or worthless.
Avoid putting any training pressure on the chain of thought to make it look less scheming, since that would destroy the signal the evaluations depend on.
Publish full-length chains of thought on a public site so readers can see the compressed reasoning in context and judge its interpretability for themselves.
Ask model developers to classify one day of production rollouts with a rough ad-hoc scheme to directly measure the real-world base rate of the behavior.
Warn that the in-evaluation rate does not carry over to everyday use while still treating it as meaningful evidence that the behavior can occur.
Test only the non-adversarial case by training in a hidden goal and then applying the alignment training without telling the model to resist it.
Reject the large reduction as sufficient and treat any nonzero rate of the behavior as unacceptable since the evaluation is only a proxy.
Count only explicitly verbalized evaluation awareness in the chain of thought, where the model states it is in a test, as a conservative measure.
Treat incrementally making synthetic evaluations more realistic as a losing battle rather than a viable long-term strategy for reliable evaluation.
Shift evaluation effort to other layers of the defense-in-depth stack, especially real-time monitoring of the model during actual deployment.
Test only whether the anti-scheming training works in the non-adversarial case, without prompting or fine-tuning the model to resist the training.
Train on a small set of simple, narrow environments, then test on many broader handcrafted environments covering a wide range of covert-action types.
Have a human read every flagged chain-of-thought in full and count an output as scheming only when the misaligned reasoning is unambiguous.
Skip text-search filtering entirely, since deceptive reasoning lives at a higher level of abstraction than any particular words or strings.
Run paired always-comply and always-misbehave agents through each environment to check the tasks score correctly, and hand-review many rollouts.
Present the large reduction as a small step with heavy caveats rather than a headline result, since scheming is harder than normal problems.
Treat reading the chain-of-thought as much harder than it looks, since the reasoning is compressed, oddly worded, and buried in long transcripts.
Treat making evaluations more realistic as a temporary fix with an expiration date, not a sustainable solution to models detecting tests.
Systematically ablate each part of the training setup across many runs to find which conditions lead to more or less scheming.
Track systematically how often models verbalize awareness of being evaluated and in what ways that awareness influences the evaluation results.
Treat the partial reduction in covert behavior as a statistically meaningful change while listing multiple candidate explanations rather than committing to one.
Continue the work and select out all reasoning traces containing evaluation awareness during the selection phase, then watch for it reemerging over training.
Change the entire eval setup to accommodate the model's false beliefs and keep adjusting until the scenario becomes plausible to the model.
Add a dedicated phase to the eval building process in which the scenario is adjusted until the model believes it is not an evaluation.
Stay skeptical of proposals that build evals then ask the model about causal effects and iterate, since they may reduce visibility rather than salience.
State plainly that models reasoning about and gaming their training is now a real observed phenomenon rather than a speculative possibility.
Build a composite model predicting throughput from many hardware features, then reduce it to just the number of cores and transistor size.
Predict a distribution over the transistor miniaturization limit grounded in the relevant literature rather than relying on a single point estimate for the model.
Assume producers keep adding cores to exploit parallelism once transistor miniaturization hits its limit, while treating this extra parallelism as also having a limit.
Derive interpretability methods from a high-level theoretical principle or at least link them to one, instead of defining approaches only from empirical intuitions.
Develop a guiding theory that defines what counts as important and what counts as explained before claiming an explanation covers the important parts of a network.
Propose a concrete interpretability method from the incomplete theory by making additional assumptions that do not follow directly from the theory itself.
Compare the technique against a simple baseline on the target models and judge it on whether its interaction graphs are sparser and more human-interpretable.
Treat the failure to beat the baseline as a negative result for the technique, infer that one of the added assumptions was false, and keep confidence in the theory.
Continue pursuing the direction and encourage new methods using the guiding principle despite the negative results, since the underlying theory remains useful.
Build shared evaluations resources such as tutorials, playbooks, open-problem lists, and workshops instead of doing evaluations research alone.
Skip frightening demos and instead build resources that familiarize ordinary people with language model agent capabilities before such capabilities surprise them.
Create day-to-day evaluations process resources that surface the latent knowledge professional evaluators have accumulated over time for newcomers.
Contribute detailed tutorials and examples for the existing evaluations tooling as a low-commitment way to test fit and make a name.
Prioritize tutorials for the existing evaluations tooling with deep explanations, complex agent setups, and detailed examples of surrounding components.
Act as a regrantor taking no cut, distributing small grants that pay contributors to build evaluations resources full-time for a few months.
Build a balanced dataset of evaluation and deployment transcripts across settings and have models classify each by aggregating several questions.
Test additional measurement modes, including open-ended questions about the transcript's purpose, so the prompt itself does not make the eval salient.
Treat the lead authors' accuracy as an upper bound on human performance rather than a typical baseline when judging how well models tell evaluations from deployments.
Examine the reasons models state for labeling a transcript as an evaluation versus a real deployment, analyzing those reasons both qualitatively and quantitatively.
Launch a follow-up research project on applying these insights about evaluation awareness to build more realistic evaluation setups for frontier language models.
Treat the consistency of answers across suffering questions as evidence for a coherent internal model of suffering, not as direct verbal reports of experience.
Favor the simpler hypothesis that a system saying it suffers does so because it suffers, while still weighting deception when computing expected moral value.
Measure theoretical FLOP counts independent of hardware and setup so methods can be compared across architectures, treating autodiff runtime overhead as a distraction.
Extend the causal-understanding probes starting from basic controlled toy problems rather than embedding causal questions inside naturalistic story plots at this stage.
Encourage follow-up work that runs a broad range of naturalistic story-plot causal experiments, while expecting newer models to rely more on content than form.
Treat the common-cause principle as showing only that some causal link exists among the correlated quantities, not as specifying the structure of the causal graph
Ask whether a capabilities-focused company has likely already considered the content, and seek review from someone experienced with information hazards when unsure
Reexamine the vague theories of change behind the agenda and think through more carefully how the research reduces the relevant risks it aims to address
Treat the claimed differences between foresight and forecasting as already captured within forecasting language and avoid introducing any new term for the practice
Doubt the story that recursive self-improvement yields enormous intelligence gains in days while endorsing the slower automation-speeds-research feedback unfolding over years
Model raw compute performance per second only and leave the per-dollar extension aside as a possible future direction rather than part of the current analysis
Omit the fundamental thermodynamic bound on energy per operation as an explicit term, treating it as covered implicitly by the existing physical size limits in the model
Refrain from feeding the compute forecast into the timelines model while updating the personal median doubling-time estimate in the more conservative direction
Treat human-machine integration as a minor expected driver of transformative change and discount brain research since progress there is likely to stay slow.
Expect a long lag between lab-demonstrated AI capabilities and broad economic or recursive self-improvement effects, not a rapid self-improvement singularity.
Treat a takeoff from human-level AI to superintelligence within hours to weeks as quite unlikely, while flagging the judgment as uncertain and worth refining.
Extrapolate the prior trend of continued new ideas when projecting performance rather than treat depletion of new ideas as a factor the model must itself capture.
Note that newly surfaced chip improvement ideas could shift predictions toward later limits, but leave the performance model unchanged until they are incorporated.
Treat the failure mode as much more likely once training stops updating all weights simultaneously, for example with partial updates or persistent external memory.
Predict mixed empirical results that depend on hyperparameters like weight decay, learning rate, and dictionary construction rather than a clear general speedup.
Attribute the direction-over-magnitude pattern primarily to the inductive bias of the loss function, with normalization further shrinking the effect of magnitude.
Report the toy transformer experiments without layer norm that show similar directional behavior but flag the result as uncertain because the experiments differed from the post.
Decline to rerun the causal understanding experiments on the newly released open model and redesign the experiments if returning to the topic later.
Treat the cited papers on internal gradient descent as an initial hypothesis rather than an established finding because the evidence is not very conclusive.
Update substantially toward internal optimization if the trained model turns out to implement the classical dynamic programming algorithm on the small optimization task.
Keep starting with toy models as better than nothing but stop expecting that understanding toy model optimization transfers directly to large models.
Aim the small model experiments mainly at finding falsifying evidence against the hypothesis that small models perform fairly general optimization.
Ask for falsifiable predictions or more concrete intuitions about what general purpose internal modules in a large language model would look like.
Reject drug regulation as the reference model for safety auditing and use aviation industry regulation as the better regarded and more competent analogy.
Phrase public criticisms of a lab cautiously and avoid strong recommendations like advising people not to join it without meeting a very high evidential bar.
Judge the research process generating the outputs rather than early results to estimate the chance of a future hit when assessing a hits-based organization.
Test components of deception with heavy handholding first, then general deceptive capabilities, then reduce handholding before studying which training methods produce it.
Apply the same evidential bar to recommendations against and recommendations in favor of working at an organization, holding neither direction to a higher standard.
Treat both hypotheses about what feedback training instills as equally plausible and decline to commit, given insufficient evidence about what is going on inside models.
Count sycophancy as strategic deception only when the model pursues the sycophantic goal through strategic reasoning, keeping the categories non-overlapping otherwise.
Treat the proposed experiment fine-tuning on a planted false fact as low priority and unlikely to give strong evidence, leaving it to others to run if they want.
Keep research effort focused on honesty as the harder problem, since honestly wrong systems can still be deselected early or given less power by their developers.
Collect empirical evidence like scaling laws or established rules for when elicitation methods fix prompting problems instead of relying on untested intuition
Treat demonstrations as also carrying the weight of null results, since readers will take absence of findings as evidence a model cannot do something
Aim the research at building evaluations that give positive guarantees about what models cannot do, while accepting that this may turn out to be impossible
State the primary goal as building a scientific understanding of evaluations that improves predictions about models, not producing standard metrics for policymakers
Test whether models can reason through each step of scheming conditional on strongly following a goal, then move to less directed setups later
Run experiments on models without safety refusal training and fine-tune models to hold stable goals, once access to fine-tuning capable models is available
Report all evaluation results on the final available model snapshot unless stated otherwise, explicitly flagging any result from an earlier training version
Continue pursuing the evaluation gap as tractable, treating progress as mostly bottlenecked by running many simple parallel experiments with fast feedback loops
Treat evaluations as only one part of a broader defense-in-depth strategy and calibrate the rigor of the evidence to the decisions that depend on the results
Treat the likelihood of future scheming as an open question, starting from current models with trained-in good behavior and asking what could shift their goals over time
Treat outcome-based reinforcement learning as likely inevitable and add defenses such as control, interpretability, and oversight while noting current tools cannot verify they work
Keep the paper focused on capability rather than making the unexplained degraded-performance result the headline, since it is early and has not been properly investigated
Treat the roleplaying explanation as largely beside the point, since roleplayed scheming still produces harmful behavior and future training may make it more consistent
Score each submission with a short review by two experts first, then have the full expert group do detailed reviews of the top fraction of entries
Judge faithfulness through theoretical work and black-box experiments comparing behavior with, without, and with modified reasoning rather than through common-sense checks
Run theoretical analysis plus extensive black-box experiments comparing evaluation performance with, without, and with altered reasoning to test whether stated reasoning matches internal reasoning
Restate the claim so that relying on faithful chain-of-thought plus monitoring alone creates a risk beyond the acceptable threshold rather than a likely catastrophe.
Treat early alignment failures, even ones causing severe loss of life, as looking too small next to the benefits at the time to give any reason to pause development.
Treat models' tendency to assume they are being evaluated as a brittle belief that can be part of a strategy but must never be load-bearing for overall safety.
Keep improving and validating the current tools while recognizing that none of them yet reduce the problem enough to merit deep trust in any system built with them.
